summary: End-to-end ML platforms provide integrated tooling for the full model lifecycle: data prep, training, fine-tuning, experiment tracking, model registry, deployment, and monitoring at scale. You need one of these platforms when you are building, customizing, or operating models in production with governance, reproducibility, and team collaboration requirements; if you simply need to call a pre-trained model (e.g., GPT, Claude, Gemini) for inference, a hosted model API is far cheaper and simpler than standing up a full MLOps platform. In 2026 the market splits between hyperscaler-native suites (SageMaker, Vertex AI, Azure ML), data-platform-led players (Databricks), and specialized best-of-breed tools (W&B, Modal, DataRobot, H2O.ai).

platforms.name: Amazon SageMaker
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go by compute/instance-hour, storage, and endpoint usage; no upfront license. Savings plans available.
platforms.best_for: Engineering-team-led purchases where AWS is the strategic cloud and native infrastructure, security, and deployment integration matter.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go by training/prediction compute, node-hours, and foundation model token usage.
platforms.best_for: Teams on Google Cloud needing strong AutoML, foundation model access, and tight BigQuery/data integration.

platforms.name: Azure Machine Learning
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go by compute/instance-hour and managed endpoint usage; enterprise agreements common.
platforms.best_for: Enterprises standardized on Microsoft/Azure with strong governance, compliance, and Azure OpenAI needs.

platforms.name: Databricks (MLflow + Mosaic AI)
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based via DBUs (Databricks Units) on top of underlying cloud compute; committed-use discounts.
platforms.best_for: Data-team-led purchases wanting unified data, analytics, ML, and GenAI with multi-cloud flexibility and governance.

platforms.name: MLflow
platforms.pricing: Free open source; managed versions billed via Databricks or cloud hosting.
platforms.best_for: Teams wanting an open, cloud-agnostic standard for experiment tracking and model registry.

platforms.name: Weights & Biases
platforms.pricing: Free tier for individuals; per-seat/usage subscription for teams and enterprise.
platforms.best_for: ML research and engineering teams needing best-in-class experiment tracking and reproducibility across any training stack.

platforms.name: DataRobot
platforms.best_for: Enterprises wanting automated ML and governed deployment with less hands-on data science effort.

platforms.name: H2O.ai
platforms.pricing: Open source core free; enterprise AutoML and GenAI via subscription/license.
platforms.best_for: Organizations wanting AutoML and open-source-friendly ML with on-prem/self-hosted options.

platforms.name: Kubeflow
platforms.pricing: Free open source; cost is underlying Kubernetes infrastructure and ops.
platforms.best_for: Platform/infra teams wanting a Kubernetes-native, cloud-agnostic MLOps stack with full control.

platforms.name: Modal
platforms.pricing: Usage-based per-second GPU/CPU billing; free starter credits.
platforms.best_for: AI startups and engineers wanting serverless GPU compute for training and inference without managing infrastructure.

platforms.name: Metaflow
platforms.pricing: Free open source; managed Outerbounds platform via subscription.
platforms.best_for: Data science teams wanting Python-native, human-friendly pipeline orchestration that scales from laptop to cloud.
